Question: Chantal and Jean start hiking from a trailhead toward a fire tower. Jean is wearing a heavy backpack and walks slower. Chantal starts walking at \(4\) miles per hour. Halfway to the tower, the trail becomes really steep, and Chantal slows down to \(2\) miles per hour. After reaching the tower, she immediately turns around and descends the steep part of the trail at \(3\) miles per hour. She meets Jean at the halfway point. What was Jean’s average speed, in miles per hour, until they meet?
Solution:
Chantal and Jean travel for the same amount of time before meeting. Let each half of the one-way trail have length \(d\) miles.

Chantal walks three segments of length \(d\): the first half at \(4\) mph, the second half at \(2\) mph, and that steep half back at \(3\) mph. Her elapsed time is
\[
\frac d4+\frac d2+\frac d3=\frac{13d}{12}\text{ hours}.
\]
Jean covers only the first half, a distance of \(d\), in that time. His average speed is therefore
\[
\frac{d}{13d/12}=\boxed{\frac{12}{13}}\text{ mph},
\]
choice A. A convenient unknown distance cancels when both travelers share the same elapsed time.
